{{Short description|American diplomat}}
[[File:Paul Wolfowitz and John Craig.jpg|thumb|John Craig (right) with Defense Secretary [[Paul Wolfowitz]] in 2001]]
'''John Bruce Craig''' (born 1945) <ref>{{cite web|url=http://politicalgraveyard.com/bio/craig.html|title=The Political Graveyard: Index to Politicians: Craig|first=Lawrence|last=Kestenbaum|website=politicalgraveyard.com}}</ref> is a native of [[Pennsylvania]].<ref name="archives.gov">{{cite web|url=https://georgewbush-whitehouse.archives.gov/news/releases/2001/10/20011023-26.html|title=Ambassador Craig Named Senior Director for Combating Terrorism|website=georgewbush-whitehouse.archives.gov}}</ref>  He served the [[United States of America]] as Special Assistant to the President and Senior Director for Combating [[Terrorism]] under [[President of the United States|President]] [[George W. Bush]].  The [[Boeing|Boeing Company]] appointed Craig to the position of Regional Vice President in the [[Middle East]], based in the [[United Arab Emirates]], with a concentration on [[Arab states of the Persian Gulf]].<ref name="skill-link.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.skill-link.com/Docs/IZ/xk_craig146.htm|title=skill-link.com|website=www.skill-link.com}}</ref> He is currently a full partner and chairman of the board for The Jadwin Consulting Group, a prominent business consulting firm based in [[Abu Dhabi]], founded by Thomas G. Finck in 2007 and focusing on business ventures and private equity opportunities in the [[Persian Gulf]] region.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ameinfo.com/153823.html |title=Jadwin Group appoints new Chairman &#124; Jadwin Group |access-date=2008-04-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080421043231/http://www.ameinfo.com/153823.html |archive-date=2008-04-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Previously, he was Ambassador to [[Oman]] from July 31, 1998, to 2001.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.congress.gov/nomination/105th-congress/1189|title=PN1189 - Nomination of John Bruce Craig for Department of State, 105th Congress (1997-1998)|date=31 July 1998|website=www.congress.gov}}</ref> Craig has also served as Director of Arabian Peninsula Affairs, [[Bureau of Near Eastern Affairs]] in the [[United States Department of State|Department of State]], Deputy Chief of Mission in Damascus, Syria and Bogota, Colombia.<ref name="archives.gov"/>

Craig holds a B.S. degree from [[American University]]'s [[School of International Service]].<ref name="archives.gov"/> He earned a master's degree in international relations from the [[National War College]] at the [[National Defense University (Washington, D.C.)|National Defense University]].

He has served as scholar-in-residence at [[Elizabethtown College]] in [[Lancaster County, Pennsylvania|Lancaster County]], [[Pennsylvania]] since October 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.etown.edu/Commencement.aspx?topic=Honorary+Degrees|title=Elizabethtown College -Page Not Found|website=www.etown.edu}}</ref>  On May 20, 2006, he received on honorary degree of Doctor of Public Service from [[Elizabethtown College]].

He was married to Gerre Lee Johnson Craig; they have one son, Jason. His wife died suddenly in 2016. <ref name="archives.gov"/>  Craig speaks French, Arabic, and Spanish.<ref name="skill-link.com"/>
